questions.title: What exactly do the "rules" produced by FeatLLM look like?
questions.question_body:
The paper talks about the large language model generating "rules" that capture conditions for each class and then converting them into new binary features. I'm not sure whether these rules are logical expressions such as `if age > 50` or more complex text snippets involving several conditions connected by AND/OR clauses.

Could you give an example of a typical rule output from GPT‑3.5 used in FeatLLM, including its format and how it maps onto code that creates a single binary feature?

questions.title: How does FeatLLM parse natural‑language rules into executable code?
questions.question_body:
The method relies on feeding the extracted textual rules back into GPT‑3 in order to generate Python code that evaluates them.

I’m worried about syntax variations such as "greater than" vs ">" or inconsistent casing for column names.

Can you explain how the prompt guarantees consistency?
Does exec() run inside a sandbox?
What happens if GPT returns syntactically incorrect code?

questions.title: Why do we fix the number of rules per class at ten?
questions.question_body:
The experiments say that each sample’s prompt asks GPT‑3 for up to 10 rules per class.

What motivated choosing this specific number?
What would change if I increased it to 20 or decreased it to 5?
Is there evidence that accuracy converges beyond ten?

questions.title: "Two‑step reasoning" – how does separating prior knowledge from data help avoid spurious correlations?
questions.question_body:
Feature generation works through Step 1 where GPT serves only prior knowledge (causal tendency) without seeing demonstrations, then Step 2 where actual examples are reviewed.

I understand intuitively this may prevent fitting noise.

Could you walk me through an example where Step 1 would infer an important feature while Step 2 still calls it out?
Does removing Step 1 increase sensitivity toward irrelevant columns?

questions.title: "Ensemble + bagging" – what exactly is being bagged here compared to a Random Forest?
questions.question_body:
FeatLLM runs multiple trials where different subsets of training instances or input columns are selected.

Is this equivalent to bootstrapping over samples only, or also over columns?

How many distinct rule sets can arise before returning final predictions?
And why does averaging logit probabilities over trials improve robustness compared with just picking one rule set?

questions.title: "Non‑negative weight constraint" – why apply `max(w_k,0)` instead of letting weights take any value?
questions.question_body:
`Equation (3) uses ReLU on w_k so all learned coefficients are positive.

Intuitively I guess preventing negative contributions protects against wrongly discarding true positives.

But metric-wise wouldn’t allowing negative values help learn hierarchy among rules?

Could you elaborate on the intuition/principle behind restricting weights

questions.title: "Binary feature creation at inference" – will I need another round through GPT‑3 when predicting new data?
questions.question_body:
"FeatLLM claims no inference cost from LLM at runtime" but manages binary flags via generated code.

During inference do we simply evaluate all our pre‑generated Python functions over every record?

Or do we rerun NLP prompting at prediction time because `parse_rules` + `exec` happen within each trial again?

questions.title: "Feature description” removal impacts all datasets – what kind of prior knowledge did you embed unused during ablative tests?
questions.question_body:
"Feature descriptions” give dimensionality/type & custom definitions.

When you removed them (`-Description`) I see larger AUC drop especially with few shots.

In practice such descriptions might not always exist – so my concern is how reliable FeatLLM is without them? How critical is having defined ranges for numeric columns versus just column names?

questions.title: "Spurious correlation experiment” – why did adding unrelated Adult columns degrade others less than baseline methods?
questions.question_body:
"Table 4 shows small impact when unrelated columns inflate dataset size”.

I’d appreciate more detail:
1️⃣ How did Step 1 prevent training item correlations on those irrelevant fields?
2️⃣ Did you observe any case where bonus random “useful” patterns appeared purely by chance?

questions.title: When should one use FeatLLM versus standard trees such as RandomForest?
questions.question_body:
Given Test AUC ranges over datasets, sometimes RandomForest catches up (especially when more shots). 

Is there a guideline/research‐based threshold such as “dimension d > 200” or “shot count < 16” under which FeatLLM always outperforms classical methods? And does it always offer better interpretability because it produces explicit Boolean predicates rather than opaque trees?
